title: Fabiola, storia di un appuntamento mancato: i cattolici e la coproduzione cinematografica italo-francese
publisher: Schermi 2 (2017), Università degli Studi di Milano (Paola Palma)
claims: Produced by Salvo D'Angelo's Universalia Film, with Franco-London Films (Deutschmeister) handling the French version; not an official co-production; Italian release 3 March 1949, French release 3 June 1949; later bought by United Artists.

Universalia, presided over by Count Giuseppe Dalla Torre of L'Osservatore Romano, was widely reported as a Vatican undertaking; the OCIC review's later correction disowned its claimed Catholic character.

CCC classification of the Italian commercial version: 'adulti con riserva'; a correction published in Morlion's name (not signed by him) in the OCIC's Revue internationale du cinéma calls the rating justly merited.
Veronese (Azione Cattolica), letter of 3 March 1949: 'molto discutibile' for its thesis and superfluous sensual material.
Morlion's proposed cuts (prolonged kisses, banquet dance, semi-nude courtesans) not made; Italian release carried only government censorship cuts.
Blasetti cut the first spoliarium at the French partner's request and supervised the French version.
French reception: broadly favourable notices praising crowd direction but noting excessive length; one critic: Fabiola becomes Christian through profane passion, more kisses of love than of peace.
Top Italian box office of its season; fourth in France.
licensing: Reference link only; no artwork permission implied.

Powell's Shakespearean bearing; naturalistic miracles; Steiger's Pilate and Ustinov's Herod praised.
